rot.means.ideia.ex1.e1: Back to king and pawn against king. You play White.
rot.means.ideia.ex1.e2: The key squares of this pawn are b6, c6 and d6. If your king reaches one of them, the pawn promotes.
rot.means.ideia.ex1.e3: So far, the tool for reaching them has been the opposition. But the opposition is a means: the goal is the key square.
rot.means.ideia.ex1.livre.fala: Keep playing as White and see how Black defends.
rot.means.ideia.ex1.livre.volta: Let's go back to the starting position. Suggest another move or click {verResposta}
rot.means.ideia.ex1.fins.capturado: The black king captured the pawn.
rot.means.ideia.ex1.fins.repeticao: The black king always blocks the way.
rot.means.ideia.ex1.fins.limite: The black king always blocks the way.
rot.means.ideia.ex1.p: White to move. Think and suggest a move, or click {verResposta}
rot.means.ideia.ex1.certo: Exactly! Your king goes straight next to the key squares.
rot.means.ideia.ex1.revela: The best is to take the king to c5, next to b6, c6 and d6, even without the opposition.
rot.means.ideia.ex1.err.d4e3.1: After this move, White no longer wins: Black can draw.
rot.means.ideia.ex1.err.d4e3.2: The black king goes to d7, next to c6 and d6. Your king stepped back and can no longer reach the key squares in time.
rot.means.ideia.ex1.err.d4e4.1: After this move, White no longer wins: Black can draw.
rot.means.ideia.ex1.err.d4e4.2: The black king goes to d6, one of the key squares, and blocks your king's path.
rot.means.ideia.ex1.err.d4d3.1: After this move, White no longer wins: Black can draw.
rot.means.ideia.ex1.err.d4d3.2: The black king goes to d6, one of the key squares, and blocks your king's path.
rot.means.ideia.ex1.err.d4c3.1: After this move, White no longer wins: Black can draw.
rot.means.ideia.ex1.err.d4c3.2: The black king goes to d6, one of the key squares, and blocks your king's path.
rot.means.ideia.ex1.err.c4c5.1: After this move, White no longer wins: Black can draw.
rot.means.ideia.ex1.err.c4c5.2: The black king goes to d7 and gets in front of the pawn in time.
rot.means.ideia.ex1.l.1: Your king is on c5, next to all three key squares. The kings are not facing each other: nobody has the opposition.
rot.means.ideia.ex1.l.2: The black king cannot guard all three at once.
rot.means.ideia.ex1.l.3: Black takes the king to d7, to guard c6 and d6.
rot.means.ideia.ex1.l.4: You go to b6, the key square left free. With the king on it, the pawn promotes.
rot.means.ideia.ex1.l.5: The black king goes to c8, in front of the pawn.
rot.means.ideia.ex1.l.6: Your king goes to c6 and controls b7, c7 and d7. The black king only has the eighth rank.
rot.means.ideia.ex1.l.7: The black king goes to b8.
rot.means.ideia.ex1.l.8: Your king goes to d7 and controls c8. Now the pawn advances on its own and promotes.
rot.means.ideia.ex1.l.9: Now compare it with the move that wins the direct opposition: the king on e4.
rot.means.ideia.ex1.l.10: Your king faces the black king, with one square between them. You have the opposition.
rot.means.ideia.ex1.l.11: But the black king goes to d6, a key square, and blocks the way. White no longer wins.
rot.means.ideia.ex1.l.12: Having the opposition did not help. First the goal: the key square. The opposition only matters if it helps you get there.
rot.means.ideia.ex1.l.13: Now let's see the defence: the black king also thinks about the goal first.
rot.means.ideia.ex2.e1: Now let's think from Black's side, and the board flips.
rot.means.ideia.ex2.e2: The pawn is on c3. Its key squares are b5, c5 and d5.
rot.means.ideia.ex2.e3: The white king, on e5, is next to d5. Your king must guard all three key squares.
rot.means.ideia.ex2.livre.fala: Keep playing as Black and see how White attacks.
rot.means.ideia.ex2.livre.volta: Let's go back to the starting position. Suggest another move or click {verResposta}
rot.means.ideia.ex2.fins.afogado: Your king was stalemated: it is a draw.
rot.means.ideia.ex2.fins.repeticao: The white king did not get through.
rot.means.ideia.ex2.fins.limite: The white king did not get through.
rot.means.ideia.ex2.p: Black to move. Think and suggest a move, or click {verResposta}
rot.means.ideia.ex2.certo: Exactly! On c6, your king guards b5, c5 and d5.
rot.means.ideia.ex2.revela: The best is to take the king to c6, next to all three key squares.
rot.means.ideia.ex2.err.d7e7.1: After this move, White can win.
rot.means.ideia.ex2.err.d7e7.2: The white king goes to d5, a key square of the pawn. With the king on it, the pawn promotes.
rot.means.ideia.ex2.err.d7c7.1: After this move, White can win.
rot.means.ideia.ex2.err.d7c7.2: The white king goes to d5, a key square of the pawn. With the king on it, the pawn promotes.
rot.means.ideia.ex2.err.d7c8.1: After this move, White can win.
rot.means.ideia.ex2.err.d7c8.2: The white king goes to d5, a key square of the pawn. With the king on it, the pawn promotes.
rot.means.ideia.ex2.err.d7d8.1: After this move, White can win.
rot.means.ideia.ex2.err.d7d8.2: The white king goes to d5, a key square of the pawn. With the king on it, the pawn promotes.
rot.means.ideia.ex2.err.d7e8.1: After this move, White can win.
rot.means.ideia.ex2.err.d7e8.2: The white king goes to d5, a key square of the pawn. With the king on it, the pawn promotes.
rot.means.ideia.ex2.l.1: Your king guards all three key squares. The kings are not facing each other, and the defence still works.
rot.means.ideia.ex2.l.2: The white king goes to d4, still next to c5 and d5.
rot.means.ideia.ex2.l.3: You face him on d6. Now the opposition helps: with it, your king guards c5, d5 and e5.
rot.means.ideia.ex2.l.4: White pushes the pawn to c4. The key squares become b6, c6 and d6.
rot.means.ideia.ex2.l.5: Your king goes to c6, in front of the pawn. It is the defence you already know, and Black draws.
rot.means.ideia.ex2.l.6: Remember: in defence, the goal is to guard the key squares. The opposition is only worth something if it helps with that.
rot.means.demos.erroDefesa.1: First position: the same as the defence, now from White's side. Black has taken the king to e7.
rot.means.demos.erroDefesa.2: The black king is facing yours, with one square between them: Black has the opposition.
rot.means.demos.erroDefesa.3: But the opposition does not guard d5, a key square of the pawn.
rot.means.demos.erroDefesa.4: Your king goes to d5, a key square. With the king on it, the pawn promotes.
rot.means.demos.erroDefesa.5: The black king faces you again, on d7.
rot.means.demos.erroDefesa.6: Now the pawn advances to c4, protected by the king.
rot.means.demos.erroDefesa.7: The black king goes to c7, in front of the pawn.
rot.means.demos.erroDefesa.8: Your king goes to c5, next to b6, c6 and d6, the new key squares. White wins.
rot.means.demos.erroDefesa.9: Black's opposition was of no use, because it did not guard the goal.
rot.means.demos.recap.1: Before practising, let's recap the ideas of this part of the lesson.
rot.means.demos.recap.2: The key square: if the king reaches it, the pawn promotes, whatever the other king does.
rot.means.demos.recap.3: The direct opposition: kings facing each other, with one square between them. Whoever just moved has it, and the other king must give way.
rot.means.demos.recap.4: Zugzwang: the side to move is forced to play and worsen its own position.
rot.means.demos.recap.5: Stalemate: a king with no moves and not in check. It is a draw.
rot.means.demos.recap.6: The opposition also works on the diagonal and on the rank, as in the defence from the game between Carlsen and So.
rot.means.demos.recap.7: The distant opposition: count the squares between the kings. An odd number after your move, and the opposition is yours.
rot.means.demos.recap.8: When the target is an enemy pawn, the king uses the opposition to go around the other king and capture it.
rot.means.demos.recap.9: With blocked pawns only the kings move, and a square watched by a pawn can decide who gets the opposition.
rot.means.demos.recap.10: And today: the opposition is the means, and the goal is the key square. If the king can reach it directly, it doesn't need the opposition.
rot.means.demos.recap.11: Your turn: one attack and one defence against the machine. Before each move, ask yourself: what is the goal?
rot.means.pratica.ataque.enunciado: Play White and find the best move.
rot.means.pratica.ataque.fim: Your king went straight to the key squares, without fighting for the opposition.
rot.means.pratica.ataque.err.e3f3.1: 1.Kf3? keeps the direct opposition, but does not get closer to c5, d5 and e5: the win slips away.
rot.means.pratica.ataque.err.e3f3.2: 1...Ke5! The black king reaches a key square first and blocks your king's path.
rot.means.pratica.ataque.err.e3f2.1: 1.Kf2? steps back, away from the key squares c5, d5 and e5: the win slips away.
rot.means.pratica.ataque.err.e3f2.2: 1...Ke5 The black king reaches a key square first and blocks your king's path.
rot.means.pratica.ataque.err.e3e2.1: 1.Ke2? steps back, away from the key squares c5, d5 and e5: the win slips away.
rot.means.pratica.ataque.err.e3e2.2: 1...Ke5 The black king reaches a key square first and blocks your king's path.
rot.means.pratica.ataque.err.e3d2.1: 1.Kd2? steps back, away from the key squares c5, d5 and e5: the win slips away.
rot.means.pratica.ataque.err.e3d2.2: 1...Ke5 The black king reaches a key square first and blocks your king's path.
rot.means.pratica.ataque.err.d3d4.1: 1.d4? pushes the pawn before the king, and the key squares become c6, d6 and e6: the win slips away.
rot.means.pratica.ataque.err.d3d4.2: 1...Ke6 The black king occupies one of the new key squares, in front of the pawn.
rot.means.pratica.defesa.enunciado: Play Black and find the best move.
rot.means.pratica.defesa.fim: Your king guarded the key squares, and the white king did not get through.
rot.means.pratica.defesa.err.e5e4.1: 1...Ke4? keeps the opposition, but moves away from the key squares c6, d6 and e6: the draw slips away.
rot.means.pratica.defesa.err.e5e4.2: 2.Kc5 The white king stands next to b6, c6 and d6, and your king cannot guard all three.
rot.means.pratica.defesa.err.e5e6.1: 1...Ke6? occupies a key square, but leaves c6 and b6 unguarded: the draw slips away.
rot.means.pratica.defesa.err.e5e6.2: 2.Kc5! The white king stands next to b6, c6 and d6, and your king cannot guard all three.
rot.means.pratica.defesa.err.e5f5.1: 1...Kf5? moves away from the key squares c6, d6 and e6: the draw slips away.
rot.means.pratica.defesa.err.e5f5.2: 2.Kd5 The white king stands next to c6, d6 and e6, and your king arrives too late.
rot.means.pratica.defesa.err.e5f6.1: 1...Kf6? moves away from c6 and d6: the draw slips away.
rot.means.pratica.defesa.err.e5f6.2: 2.Kd5 The white king stands next to c6, d6 and e6, and your king arrives too late.
rot.means.pratica.defesa.err.e5f4.1: 1...Kf4? moves away from the key squares c6, d6 and e6: the draw slips away.
rot.means.pratica.defesa.err.e5f4.2: 2.Kd5 The white king stands next to c6, d6 and e6, and your king arrives too late.
